_timing: Beat durations are cut to the narration's own pauses, measured with ffmpeg silencedetect on sounds/konami-keen.mp3 (-35dB, 0.30s). The voice's six speech segments end at 1.784 / 3.997 / 9.710 / 17.669 / 22.561 / 24.189s. The narration is then held back by voiceDelayInFrames so the opening code beat can finish typing in silence before anyone speaks; every boundary below is a segment end plus that delay. Cuts land within ~20ms of the speaker's sentence breaks, so the picture changes where the voice breathes. Re-measure and re-cut all of this if the narration is ever regenerated.

beats.lead: But here is the part nobody says
beats.text: It was never meant to ship.
beats.note: The Konami Code was debug scaffolding. It was supposed to be deleted before release.

beats.name: Kazuhisa Hashimoto
beats.role: Porting Gradius to the NES. He could not get through his own game well enough to test it, so he wrote a shortcut that handed the player every power-up at once.

beats.context: What the same code granted in Contra, two years later. That is the version most people remember.

beats.text: He forgot to take it out.

beats.line: A bug that outlived the console.
